request.spec:
A steward can merge a person into another (a select of the other person and a merge button on
the row; PERSON_MERGED from=<name> into=<name>; anyone else, the same person, or either of them
retired, is refused with an error on the row). The merged person's claims move to the other
(numbers and dates kept, listed after the other's claims in the order they were added, each losing
any figure a statement bound); the merged name and aliases become aliases of the other; the merged
person's patrons are added to the other's (not themselves, no repeats), anyone naming the merged
person as patron names the other instead (no repeats), and the merged person's pool memberships move
to the other (shares added when the other is already a member). Their statements, holds, watchers
and contact are dropped. The merged person leaves the list (no row), and every total follows.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can merge a person into another (a select of the other person and a merge button on
the row; PERSON_MERGED from=<name> into=<name>; anyone else, the same person, or either of them
retired, is refused with an error on the row). The merged person's claims move to the other
(numbers and dates kept, listed after the other's claims in the order they were added, each losing
any figure a statement bound); the merged name and aliases become aliases of the other; the merged
person's patrons are added to the other's (not themselves, no repeats), anyone naming the merged
person as patron names the other instead (no repeats), and the merged person's pool memberships move
to the other (shares added when the other is already a member). Their statements, holds, watchers
and contact are dropped. The merged person leaves the list (no row), and every total follows.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Stewards can now merge one person into another, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests (the main merge test and the three scenario tests).

**On screen:** each person row has a new "Merge" cell with a `person-merge-into` select listing everyone on the sheet, a `person-merge` button, and a `person-error` message when the merge is refused. The person themselves is in the list on purpose, so that choosing them gets refused by the server with an error rather than not being possible. After a merge, everything on the sheet reloads, so totals, pools, claims and statements all update.

**On the server:** a new endpoint, `PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/merge` with body `{ intoId }`, built in the same style as the retire and statement endpoints. The work is done in `person/ApplyMerge.java`:
- **Refused:** if the user isn't a steward (a delegated steward counts), if it's the same person, or if either person is retired. Nothing is written in that case.
- **Claims** move to the other person in the order they were added. Each keeps its number and date, loses any figure a statement bound, and is listed as the other person's newest.
- **Name and aliases:** the merged person's name, then their aliases, become aliases of the other person.
- **Patrons:** the merged person's patrons are added to the other's, and anyone who named the merged person now names the other. Self-references and repeats are dropped.
- **Pools:** memberships move to the other person, and shares are added together where they're already a member.
- **Dropped:** statements, watchers, holds and contact. I also drop the merged person's dated grades, which the request didn't mention. Then the person is deleted, which the existing history recording picks up for the as-of views.
- **Audit:** writes `PERSON_MERGED sheet=… by=… from=<name> into=<name>`, followed by the usual ROLLUP and TOTALS lines when figures change.

**Supporting changes:** setters on `PoolMember`, two new lookups (pool memberships by person, and who names a given person as patron), and the new files `ValidateMerge`, `MergeInput`, `PersonMerged`, `AuditPersonMerged`, `RespondWithMergedInto` and `features/people/merge.slot.tsx`.

Two kinds of old records stay attached to the merged person's id: closed periods' stored per-person totals, and statement binding logs. Neither shows up on screen or in the test.
